colour_mood: A warm off-white reading surface (#FAF8F4) is the ground of the site — comfortable for long guides and articles. Charcoal and near-black are used only for the chrome that frames it: header, footer, hero, and panels that show a system doing something. One accent, a dark antique gold, used sparingly for links and controls on the light surface. This is NOT a dark theme; it is a light reading surface with dark chrome.

specialised_slots._note: NOT core slots — the theme palette wins these, so they live on the forked palette 'leopardess-dark-gold' (leopardess-owned; the seed 3196d966 dresses 4 sites and must never be edited). Values here mirror that palette. All pairs WCAG-validated 2026-07-10.
specialised_slots.heading: #0D0D0D

typography.character: A single geometric sans (Inter), differentiated by weight and size, body large enough for long-form reading.
typography.guidance: Use these values verbatim; do not introduce a serif or a second family.

typography_mood: A single geometric sans across headings and body, differentiated by weight and size rather than by mixing families. Body text large enough to read a long guide without effort. Monospace only for things that are literally code or identifiers, never for atmosphere.

logo.concept: A stylised leopardess head in profile, reduced to a few confident strokes of a single weight. Spots implied by their arrangement rather than drawn in full. It must survive being shrunk to a 16px favicon and must read as one shape at that size.
logo.treatment: Flat. One colour on transparent. No gradient, no bevel, no glow, no three-quarter perspective, no photographic rendering, no eyes that follow you.
logo.usage: One logo for the life of the site: header, favicon, and social cards, all derived from the same file. It becomes the reference image for every other image the site generates, which is how the graphic language stays one family.

imagery_direction: Two families, kept apart on purpose. Explanatory images — how a pipeline flows, what a work item is, where a person approves a step — are diagrams: flat, gold on charcoal, drawn in the same hand as the logo. Charts of real data are never generated by an image model, because an image model draws the appearance of a chart and invents the numbers. Charts are rendered by code from a real series, and they carry their source and the date the figure was taken. Photographs of people in offices, handshakes, glowing brains, robot faces, and neural-network filigree have no place here.
layout_preference: Room to breathe. Cards in threes on a wide screen, dropping to two and then one, and never leaving a single stretched orphan on the last row. If the content does not divide into threes, that is usually the content telling you two of the cards are saying the same thing. Long-form pages get a comfortable measure and a light background. Hero sections carry one clear sentence, not three competing ones. Calls to action are specific and quiet.
avoid: Stock photography of any kind, and portraits of people who do not exist
Charts produced by an image generator, under any circumstances
Decorative animation, parallax, and anything that delays the first paragraph being readable
Testimonial carousels, client logo walls, and social proof we have not earned
Dense grids with no whitespace, and cards that repeat their neighbour's point in different words
Any visual element whose purpose is to look like technology rather than to explain something
_superseded: The previous design_intent banned literal leopard imagery ('the brand metaphor is applied through language, not visuals'). The owner overrode this on 2026-07-09: the site gets a real leopardess mark. The previous spec also claimed style_direction 'professional-dark' while setting a #ffffff background, which is the contradiction that produced the current mismatched site.
brand_gold: #C8A951 — the leopardess gold. It lives ONLY on dark grounds (logo, header, hero, the CTA fill), where it scores 8.56:1. As link text on the light reading surface it scores 2.14:1 and fails WCAG AA, so the functional `accent` is the darker bronze #836E32 (4.67 on the page, 4.95 on a card). Two-tone by necessity, not decoration. Do not 'restore' the bright gold to `accent`.

palette.character: Dark charcoal chrome around warm off-white reading surfaces. One antique gold, used sparingly and only where it means something.
palette.guidance: These eight values are FIXED and non-negotiable. They are the brand's WCAG-AA-validated palette and every pair has already been contrast-checked. Output them VERBATIM in color_scheme — do not adjust any hue, saturation or lightness, and do not substitute a darker background or a brighter accent. In particular: background MUST be #FAF8F4 (a warm off-white reading surface, NOT a dark theme), text MUST be #1A1A1A (near-black), and accent MUST be #836E32 (a dark bronze — the bright brand gold #C8A951 fails AA on this light surface and must NOT be used as the accent). This site is deliberately a light-reading-surface design with dark chrome supplied separately by specialised palette slots; do not turn it into a dark theme.
